brief: Limits approval — the product's signature screen. A person sets four plain-language limits on what Modalis may do with their money, sees the consequence of each one in dollars as they move it, previews a bad year, and approves. Approval is the moment the plan goes live, so the screen is treated as a signing ceremony rather than a settings form. Same content and same four limits in every direction; only the visual and interaction language changes.

candidates.name: Current
candidates.concept: What ships today: rounded cards on a warm white page, limits as a read-only list, lime accent on the action.
candidates.typography: Monda 700 for headings, Geist 400/500/600 for everything else, tabular figures for money

candidates.name: Ledger
candidates.concept: This is a financial instrument, so make it read like one. Hairline rules, a fixed grid, every consequence sitting in its own column — the density itself is the reassurance.
candidates.typography: Geist 400/500/600 for text, Geist Mono for every number, 34px tight headline
traits: two-column rows: control left, consequence right

candidates.name: Corridor
candidates.concept: A limit is a room to move in, so draw the room. Each limit is a band with your line inside it — the central metaphor of the product made literal and reused on Home.
candidates.typography: Geist 600 at 46px tight for display, Geist Mono for amounts, generous line height
traits: each limit drawn as a band you sit inside
one accent marks your position and the primary action
carries straight into the Home corridor

candidates.name: Editorial
candidates.concept: People sign what they have read. Set each limit as a sentence with the number in it, in a serif, with the consequence in the margin like a footnote.
candidates.typography: Georgia serif at 62px for display and headings, Geist for UI, Geist Mono for labels
traits: limits read as sentences, not controls
